headline: Compare a fixed-width window to the target counts
statement: Return whether string s2 contains a contiguous substring that is a permutation of s1. Matching requires identical character multiplicities, regardless of order.
prerequisites: Basic Python lists, loops, and functions
constraints: Both strings contain lowercase English letters.
intuition: All permutations have the same length and frequency vector. Slide a window of exactly len(s1) through s2, adding the arriving letter and subtracting the departing letter. Compare 26 counters instead of constructing permutations.
approach: Update a 26-entry window count while scanning s2.
Once the window exceeds the target width, remove its old left letter.
For each full-width window, compare the two vectors.
correctness: At right index r, window counts describe exactly the last len(s1) characters once enough characters exist. Two equal-length strings are permutations precisely when all letter counts agree. Every candidate substring of that length is scanned, so returning true is equivalent to a permutation occurring.
bruteForce: Generate all permutations of s1 and search each in s2, costing factorial work and duplicating permutations when letters repeat.

complexity.explanation: Comparing 26 counters is constant work per window; the alphabet size is fixed.

pitfalls: The window length is fixed, not variable.
Multiplicity matters; a set cannot distinguish aa from ab.
If s1 is longer than s2, the answer is false.
